reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: AI-powered weapons and human decision
themes.definition: Concern over AI-powered weapons and autonomous systems, with calls for international frameworks analogous to WMD regimes.
themes.inclusion: Include references to AI-powered weapons, autonomous systems on the battlefield, or machines making life-or-death decisions.
themes.exclusion: Exclude AI security challenges unrelated to weapons.
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for frameworks modelled on nuclear/chemical/biological weapons rules are coded here and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: machines should never be allowed to make life-or-death decisions on their own

themes.label: AI concentrated among few creates divisions
themes.definition: Unequal access to AI risks benefiting only the strongest economies and biggest companies and leaving communities behind.
themes.inclusion: Include warnings that AI access inequality will create new divisions between countries or communities.
themes.exclusion: Exclude statements about concentration of power without access consequences (code AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
themes.boundary_cases: Mentions of 'biggest companies' capturing benefits may also be coded AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: If AI is available only to a few, new divisions will appear.

themes.label: AI harming education and youth
themes.definition: AI is framed as already negatively affecting education and a generation of young people, and as a topic for education-focused summits.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI's impact on learning, test scores, youth, or AI-and-education initiatives.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general education passages without AI.
themes.boundary_cases: Hosting an education-and-AI summit also reflects AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY leadership.

examples.quote: It is already having a negative impact on society, especially in education.
hosting all the actors at the Summit on Education and AI in Bratislava

themes.label: AI as tool for peace and prevention
themes.definition: AI is presented as a potential tool for diplomacy, mediation and conflict prevention through analysis, pattern recognition and translation.
themes.inclusion: Include passages proposing AI use for peacebuilding, mediation, early warning or conflict prevention.
themes.exclusion: Exclude generic development benefits of AI (code AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS).
themes.boundary_cases: Passages that use AI only as a metaphor for institutional reform are not coded here.

examples.quote: It can be also a tool for peace. It can help us analyze information, identify patterns, and overcome language barriers in real time.
we can move this technology away from the battlefield and towards diplomacy, mediation, and conflict prevention

themes.label: Responsible approach and international frameworks
themes.definition: Calls for strong international frameworks and a responsible multi-stakeholder approach to fast-moving AI, with a UN lead role.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for international AI rules or responsible approaches by institutions, private sector and governments.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages only mentioning AI as a metaphor.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements that the UN should lead may also be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: We also need strong international frameworks for these new technologies. The United Nations can and should play a leading role in this effort.
We need a responsible approach from all international institutions, the private sector, and also the governments.

value.rationale: Slovakia's passages offer a multi-faceted AI discussion: access inequality, AI weapons, harm to education, and AI as a tool for peace, alongside calls for international frameworks; one passage uses AI mainly as a metaphor for institutional reform.
